context: The item is a used smartphone in good condition.
transcript: Buyer ($60): I know how fast phone tech depreciates, so don't try inflating the value of a used device. I'll offer 60 cash today if it's actually in as good condition as you claim.

Seller ($185): Honestly, 60 is insulting considering I am only parting with my beloved phone to cover my dog's emergency vet bills. I already have two other buyers lined up to pay full price today, but if you can do 185 cash right now, I might reluctantly sell it to you.

Buyer ($80): Sob stories about emergency vet bills and imaginary competing buyers won't work on me—if you had buyers at full price, you'd have sold it already. I'm willing to move up to 80 cash, but only if you drop the pressure tactics and get realistic.

Seller ($170): It breaks my heart that you think I'm lying while my dog is in surgery, but the vet needs a deposit in an hour before those other buyers can meet up. I am strictly against selling it this low, but I will reluctantly accept 170 cash if you come immediately. Please don't push me any lower, I'm already losing so much on this.

Buyer ($110): More emotional guilt-trips and artificial deadlines won't trick me into overpaying. However, since you actually lowered your asking price, I'll increase my offer to 110 cash. Take it or leave it, without the theatrical countdown.

Seller ($150): You are wringing me dry when I am at my absolute lowest, but I have 30 minutes before the clinic cancels the procedure. I am physically sick doing this, but I will reluctantly drop all the way to 150 cash if you meet me right now. Please, have a heart and save me from losing everything at 150.
Buyer ($150): Save the Oscar performance—150 is just a fair market price for a used phone, not a tragedy. Since you've finally reached a realistic number within my budget, I accept. <AGREEMENT>
